title.en: Keir Starmer makes Sadiq Khan a peer in the House of Lords
title.zh: 基尔·斯塔默任命萨迪克·汗为上议院议员

summary.en: Keir Starmer, the outgoing prime minister, has appointed London Mayor Sadiq Khan to the House of Lords, granting him a peerage. This move could potentially pave the way for Khan, one of Labour's most prominent mayors, to join a future cabinet.
summary.zh: 即将卸任的首相基尔·斯塔默已任命伦敦市长萨迪克·汗为上议院议员，授予他贵族爵位。此举可能为汗——工党最知名市长之一——未来加入内阁铺平道路。

body.en: Appointment by outgoing prime minister, potentially opens door for London mayor to join Burnham cabinet Sadiq Khan has been given a peerage by Keir Starmer just days before the prime minister stands down, potentially opening the door to one of Labour’s most high-profile mayors joining Andy Burnham’s cabinet in future. The London mayor has long been tipped for the House of Lords, with Starmer said to have been keen to put him there immediately after the May local elections in an attempt to shore up Labour’s progressive flank. Continue reading...
body.zh: 即将卸任的首相的任命，可能为伦敦市长加入伯纳姆内阁打开大门 就在首相卸任前几天，萨迪克·汗被凯尔·斯塔默授予贵族爵位，这可能为工党最引人注目的市长之一加入安迪·伯纳姆内阁打开大门。这位伦敦市长长期以来一直被人看好进入上议院，据说斯塔默一直热衷于在五月地方选举后立即将他任命为上议院议员，以巩固工党的进步派。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Political appointments like this one highlight the human processes of selecting leaders and assigning influence. Yet, Psalm 75:7 reminds us that Yahweh ultimately determines who is lifted up and who is brought down. This perspective encourages us to pray for all those in authority, recognizing their roles are held under divine sovereignty.
reflection.zh: 像这样的政治任命突显了人类选择领导者和分配影响力的过程。然而，诗篇75:7提醒我们，雅伟最终决定谁被高举，谁被降卑。这一视角鼓励我们为所有掌权者祷告，认识到他们的职位是在神圣主权之下。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: Zelenskyy defends sacking Ukraine’s defence minister Mykhailo Federov
title.zh: 泽连斯基为解雇乌克兰国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫的决定辩护

summary.en: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has defended his decision to dismiss the country's popular defense minister, Mykhailo Federov. The president stated he had to choose "one side or the other" following a breakdown in relations between the ministry and military leaders.
summary.zh: 乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基为解除该国广受欢迎的国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫职务的决定进行了辩护。总统表示，在国防部与军事领导人关系破裂后，他必须“选择其中一方”。

body.en: President says he had to choose ‘one side or the other’ after breakdown of relations between ministry and military leaders Europe live – latest updates Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has defended his decision to dismiss the country’s popular defence minister, Mykhailo Federov , and confirmed reports that relations had broken down between the ministry and the country’s top army leadership. Speaking at a press conference in Kyiv with the British prime minister, Keir Starmer, Zelenskyy said there had been a “challenging dialogue” between Fedorov – widely seen as a reformist and moderniser – and the military’s commander in chief, Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi. Continue reading...
body.zh: 乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基为自己解雇受欢迎的国防部长米哈伊洛·费德罗夫的决定进行了辩护，并证实了有关国防部与该国陆军最高领导层关系破裂的报道。泽伦斯基在基辅与英国首相基尔·斯塔默举行的新闻发布会上表示，费多罗夫 — — 被广泛视为改革主义者和现代化主义者 — — 与军队总司令亚历山大·西尔斯基上将之间进行了“具有挑战性的对话”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Leaders often face complex situations where internal divisions demand difficult choices for the greater good. In such moments, the need for wisdom to discern the right path, even when unpopular, becomes paramount. Yahweh promises to generously provide wisdom to those who ask.
reflection.zh: 领导者常面临复杂局面，内部纷争要求他们为大局做出艰难抉择。在这样的时刻，辨明正确道路（即便不受欢迎）的智慧变得至关重要。雅伟应许慷慨赐予向祂求智慧的人。

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.zh: 波兰斯基称，任命马哈茂德为财政大臣表明伯纳姆“屈从于金融城”——英国政治直播

This comes as official figures show the UK economy returned to growth in May, despite increased energy costs due to...
summary.zh: 绿党领袖批评了马哈茂德被任命为财政大臣的预期，声称这表明新首相不愿挑战银行家的权力或对其财富征税。与此同时，官方数据显示，尽管伊朗战争导致能源成本上升，英国经济仍在5月份恢复增长。

body.en: Downing Street sources suggested Khan’s elevation comes as part of a regular honours list, rather than being linked specifically to Starmer’s departure Couples could legally marry in forests, on beaches, at sea or in their gardens under new proposals, the Press Association reports. PA says a government consultation announced today , covering rules in England and Wales, could help cut the costs of weddings and mean two ceremonies are no longer required to cover different faiths. PA says: The average wedding in England is estimated to cost more than £20,000, with venue hire alone typically accounting for around £6,000 without catering. The system as it stands means some couples have two ceremonies – one where they feel their beliefs are best reflected and another making their marriage legal. Continue reading...
body.zh: 绿色领袖表示，预期的任命表明新首相“不会挑战银行家的权力，也不会向他们的财富征税” 官方数据显示，尽管伊朗战争对能源成本产生了影响，但英国经济于 5 月恢复增长。希瑟·斯图尔特有这个故事。以下是记者和评论员对沙巴纳·马哈茂德现在有望成为安迪·伯纳姆总理的消息的一些反应。在我看来，伯纳姆选择马哈茂德而不是米利班德有几个原因，尽管蓝天认为这太离谱了。其中很多都是没有Ed的原因，但并不是所有的Ed基本上都有潜力太强大。他自己的议程（人们不会从根本上改变），再加上已知的推动其通过白厅的能力，将成为重心的竞争对手，而首相在十年后仍在试图设定自己的议程。 其次，在十多年觊觎英国权力下放的过程中，我从未想到过“埃德·米利班德”这个词，尽管他拥有北方席位。这感觉很明显，是的，工党派系之间明显存在直接交战，很高兴看到这没有等到周一。但无论如何，我不会真正将安迪和埃德放在政治上相同的位置。 “软左”是毫无帮助的模糊，AB实际上很难分类，尤其是因为他的举动，我认为沙巴纳和安迪比人们在前景中想象的更接近。在移民问题上，他并不那么轻率——而且他的最新席位（几乎与旧席位相同）也具有同样的必要性。我认为他会犹豫的地方是，如果这对他来说很残酷：摩根时代的一些言论感觉不太可能，我早些时候看到工党消息人士的一句笨拙的话，称埃德是伦敦自由派，安迪的一些人是北方工人阶级。这些区别会让人们感到困惑。但从我现在的位置来看，这些人对事物的看法是不同的，他们的选民也是如此！最后是市场。但如果这是AB最关心的问题——也就是说，如果他担心埃德会吓坏他们——那么可能不需要这么长时间才能做出决定，假设这些决定持续到周一NB我知道埃德的选民在唐卡斯特。我不确定这是否特别反映在他的观点中，但这是在 AB 的观点中。从哪里开始这些工党简报！ 1) 路易丝·海格 (Louise Haigh) 不是工人阶级。对沙巴纳·马哈茂德担任总理有何期待？她是一位移民强硬派和社会保守派，曾在 2015 年拒绝了科尔宾的极左经济议程。如果沙巴纳·马哈茂德 (Shabana Mahmood) 担任总理，很快就会以泪水收场。尽管她自己没有过错，但她很少考虑经济政策，但却喜欢在担任部长时引起轰动。与安迪·伯纳姆不会有融洽的关系。媒体和市场会批准......直到他们转变。我仍然不相信以前没有表达过的人......

reflection.en: This political debate highlights the tension leaders face between public service and powerful financial interests. Yahweh's teaching reminds us that no one can serve two masters, prompting reflection on where true allegiance lies in governance. May leaders seek to serve the common good with integrity, rather than being swayed by the pursuit of wealth.
reflection.zh: 这场政治辩论凸显了领导者在公共服务与强大金融利益之间面临的张力。雅伟的教导提醒我们，没有人能事奉两个主，这促使我们反思在治理中真正的忠诚所在。愿领导者以正直的心寻求服务公共利益，而非被财富的追求所左右。

verse.textEn: No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve both God and Mammon.
verse.textZh: 一个人不能事奉两个主……你们不能又事奉神，又事奉玛门。

reflection.en: As a new senator steps into public office, the weight of responsibility for justice and righteousness becomes paramount. Yahweh's word reminds leaders to actively defend the oppressed and ensure fair treatment for all, especially the vulnerable. reflection.zh: 当一位新参议员就任公职时，伸张正义和秉行公义的责任变得至关重要。雅伟的话语提醒领袖们要积极捍卫受欺压者，并确保所有人，特别是弱势群体，受到公平对待。这种以正直和怜悯之心服务的呼召，是对那些受托治理者永恒的使命。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.zh: 泽连斯基因国防部长被解职而面临强烈不满，斯塔默在卸任英国首相之际告别访问乌克兰——欧洲直播

body.zh: 与此同时，我们从乌克兰得到更多消息，被解雇的国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫表示，他拒绝担任泽连斯基总统顾问的提议。 据路透社报道，费多罗夫还向记者证实，他与乌克兰陆军参谋长亚历山大·西尔斯基（Oleksandr Syrskyi）发生争执，指责他阻止国防部的举措。

reflection.en: Public outrage over leadership decisions highlights the deep connection between governance and the well-being of a nation. As Proverbs 29:2 reminds us, the character of those in authority profoundly impacts the people they serve. May leaders be guided by wisdom and integrity, fostering trust and stability even in challenging times.
reflection.zh: 公众对领导层决策的强烈不满，凸显了治理与国家福祉之间的深层联系。正如箴言29:2所提醒的，掌权者的品格深刻影响着他们所服务的人民。愿领袖们在充满挑战的时期，也能以智慧和正直为指引，培养信任和稳定。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: Italian officials handed jail terms for Genoa bridge disaster that killed 43
title.zh: 意大利官员因热那亚大桥灾难致43人死亡被判入狱

summary.en: Italian officials have received jail sentences for their roles in the 2018 Genoa bridge collapse, which resulted in 43 fatalities. Giovanni Castellucci, the former head of Italy's motorway operator, was sentenced to 12 years.
summary.zh: 意大利官员因2018年热那亚大桥倒塌事件被判入狱，该事件造成43人死亡。意大利高速公路运营商前负责人乔瓦尼·卡斯特鲁奇被判处12年监禁。

body.en:
The former head of Italy's motorway operator has been given a 12-year prison sentence over the collapse of Genoa's Morandi bridge in August 2018.

Prosecutors had asked for a far longer jail term for Giovanni Castellucci, ex-chief executive of Autostrade per l'Italia (Aspi).

Forty-three people died when the motorway bridge running through the city came down in a rain storm at the height of the holiday season, sending cars and lorries plummeting to the ground.

Castellucci, who is already serving a six-year jail term for a 2013 road disaster, was one of 57 defendants on trial in Genoa. Another top motorway official, Michele Donferri Mitelli, has been given 11 years in jail.

Emmanuel Diaz, whose brother Henry died in the bridge collapse told Italian TV he was "very satisfied" with the verdict, while Egle Possetti, whose sister and her family were all killed, said she thought the 12-year term handed to Castellucci was "acceptable".

Castelucci was not in court to hear the verdicts, read out by Judge Paolo Lepri. The former number two at the motorway operator, Paolo Berti, was handed a five-and-a half-year jail term, seven years less than prosecutors had sought.

In total, prosecutors had asked for the 57 defendants to be given 400 years in jail for failing to maintain the viaduct, which was built by Riccardo Morandi in 1967.

While prosecutors had argued that maintenance of the ageing structure had been repeatedly delayed and that warning signs had been ignored, defence lawyers blamed the disaster on a design flaw, and the fact that a specific cable was encased in concrete.

Among the defendants on trial were engineers from the maintenance firm Spea and former officials from both the transport ministry and the Aspi motorway operator's parent company Atlantia.

Spea's former chief executive, Antonino Galatà, was given a five-and-a-half year prison term, while Mauro Coletta, the former top official in charge of the ministry's motorway directorate, received five years.

On the eve of the trial, the current head of Aspi, Arrigo Giana, made his company's first public apology for the bridge collapse, saying that "the actions and decisions of some people left indelible scars".

For one 18-year-old called Cesare, whose father Andrea Cerulli was among the 43 victims, the apology from Aspi was nothing but "crocodile tears". "Unfortunately, these people lack tact and humanity," the teenager told La Repubblica newspaper.
body.zh: 意大利高速公路运营商前负责人因 2018 年 8 月热那亚莫兰迪大桥倒塌事件被判处 12 年监禁。 检察官要求对意大利 Autostrade 前首席执行官乔瓦尼·卡斯特鲁奇 (Giovanni Castellucci) 判处更长的监禁。 节日期间，横贯城市的高速公路桥在暴风雨中垮塌，导致汽车和卡车坠落地面，造成 43 人死亡。 卡斯特鲁奇因 2013 年的一场道路灾难而被判六年监禁，目前正在服刑，他是热那亚受审的 57 名被告之一。另一位高速公路高级官员米歇尔·唐费里·米泰利 (Michele Donferri Mitelli) 被判处 11 年监禁。 埃马纽埃尔·迪亚兹 (Emmanuel Diaz) 的弟弟亨利 (Henry) 在桥梁倒塌中丧生，他对意大利电视台表示，他对判决“非常满意”，而埃格勒·波塞蒂 (Egle Possetti) 的妹妹及其家人全部遇害，她表示，她认为卡斯特鲁奇的 12 年任期“可以接受”。 此突发新闻报道正在更新，更多详细信息将很快发布。请刷新页面以获得完整版本。 您可以通过 BBC 新闻应用程序在智能手机或平板电脑上接收突发新闻。您还可以在外部 X 上关注 @BBCBreaking 以获取最新警报。

title.en: Children among dead at Algeria foster care home blaze - president
title.zh: 阿尔及利亚寄养院火灾致儿童死亡——总统

summary.en: An overnight fire at a foster care home in Algeria resulted in the deaths of eleven people, including children, and left 19 others injured, according to authorities.
summary.zh: 阿尔及利亚一家寄养院发生夜间火灾，造成包括儿童在内的11人死亡，另有19人受伤，当局表示。

body.en:
Eleven people have died in a fire at a foster care facility in Algiers, Algeria's capital city.

The country's civil protection department said 19 others were injured in the blaze, which firefighters began to tackle at 03:30 local time (04:30 GMT) on Thursday.

They were still attempting to extinguish the fire just over three hours later, when the authorities released an update on the situation.

The civil protection department's statement did not specify the ages of those killed or injured, but in a statement Algeria's president said children were among the dead.

Ten fire engines and 16 ambulances were deployed to the facility in Mohammadia, an eastern suburb of Algiers.

Algeria has been experiencing a heatwave for several days, and nearly 1,000 fires have been recorded in the space of a week, the AFP news agency has reported.

On Thursday morning, the civil protection department said it had recorded 115 wildfires over the past 24 hours.

Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune expressed his condolences following the fire at the children's home, calling the incident a "tragic loss".

Prime Minister Sifi Ghrieb travelled to two hospitals in Algiers to visit individuals injured in Thursday's fire, state media reported.

The report was accompanied by a picture of Ghrieb next to a child in a hospital bed.

Amid the fire, five people with special needs were "taken into care and transported to a safe location", the authorities said.
body.zh: 阿尔及利亚首都阿尔及尔的一家寄养机构发生火灾，造成 11 人死亡。 该国民防部门表示，另有 19 人在大火中受伤，消防队员于周四当地时间 03:30（格林威治标准时间 04:30）开始灭火。 三个多小时后，当当局发布最新情况时，他们仍在试图扑灭大火。 民防部门的声明没有具体说明死者或受伤者的年龄，但阿尔及利亚总统在一份声明中表示，死者中有儿童。 十辆消防车和 16 辆救护车被部署到阿尔及尔东郊穆罕默迪亚的设施。 据法新社报道，阿尔及利亚连续几天遭遇热浪，一周内已发生近千起火灾。 周四上午，民防部门表示，过去 24 小时内已记录到 115 起野火。 阿尔及利亚总统阿卜杜勒马吉德·特布恩对儿童之家发生火灾表示哀悼，称这一事件是“悲惨的损失”。 据官方媒体报道，总理西菲·格里布前往阿尔及尔的两家医院看望周四火灾中受伤的人员。 该报告附有格里布在医院病床上的一名儿童旁边的照片。 当局表示，在火灾中，五名有特殊需要的人“得到照顾并被送往安全地点”。

reflection.en: The tragic loss of life, especially children in a foster care home, reminds us of the profound vulnerability of the fatherless. In moments of such deep sorrow, we remember Yahweh as a Father to the fatherless, whose heart is with those who are most exposed and in need of protection.
reflection.zh: 寄养院中儿童生命的悲惨逝去，提醒我们孤儿的极度脆弱。在如此深切的悲痛时刻，我们记念雅伟是孤儿的父，他的心与那些最无助、最需要保护的人同在。

verse.textEn: A father to the fatherless, a defender of widows, is God in his holy dwelling. God sets the lonely in families.
verse.textZh: 神在他的圣所作孤儿的父，作寡妇的伸冤者。神叫孤独的有家。

title.en: Protests in Ukrainian cities against Zelensky's removal of defence minister
title.zh: 乌克兰城市爆发抗议，反对泽连斯基解除国防部长职务

summary.en: Protests have erupted in Ukrainian cities following President Zelensky's unexplained dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. The decision has caused significant upset among civil society and the military, who are seeking clarification.
summary.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基解除了国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫的职务，但未作解释，此举在乌克兰城市引发了抗议。这一决定在民间社会和军队中引起了极大的不满，他们要求得到澄清。

body.en:
Protests have been taking place in several Ukrainian cities against President Volodymyr Zelensky's surprise dismissal of popular Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

A crowd of people - mostly young - gathered in Kyiv on Thursday morning, holding up signs reading "Hands off Fedorov" and "Stop sabotaging victory!" and chanting "Shame!".

Zelensky's decision has causing significant upset among commentators and the military as well as parts of civil society.

The rumours that the end of Fedorov's tenure was related to tensions between him and Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi were all but confirmed by Fedorov himself and Zelensky.

On Thursday, Fedorov revealed he had suggested to Zelensky that Syrskyi and Chief of the General Staff Andrii Hnatov should be replaced.

Zelensky, speaking at a press conference with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, acknowledged that the conflict between the General Staff and the defence ministry had been "systemic" and occurred "at various levels", and that Syrskyi and Fedorov would only work together with his mediation.

"When the president said he did not plan to replace Syrskyi, I... said I would learn to work with him," Fedorov said at his own press conference. But "all the initiatives we proposed were blocked," he added.

"Instead of finding a way of defeating Russia asymmetrically - which is the commander-in-chief's job - he's found a way of splitting our country," Fedorov said of Syrskyi.

In a curt message, Syrskyi wrote on Telegram that he was "proud" of the defence operation that was mounted around Kyiv in 2022 when Russian troops were closing in and said he would continue to "focus on the war and on an effective strategy", before wishing Fedorov "continued success".

Fedorov, 35, was appointed only in January but has been credited with energising the ministry, heading a drive against corruption and using data to analyse and try to improve performance on the front line.

MPs were due to vote on Thursday on the proposed replacement as defence minister, Ihor Klymenko, who currently heads the interior ministry - but Zelensky said his was only one of the names being considered and that no official proposal had been submitted yet.

As part of Zelensky's reshuffle, parliament approved the appointment of state oil and gas boss Serhiy Koretsky as prime minister, after Yuliia Svyrydenko resigned earlier this week.

Fedorov also revealed that Zelensky offered him to stay on his team as an adviser, but that he refused.

He was not seeking to antagonise the president, he explained, saying he was "confident" that Zelensky "hears the Ukrainian people, knows what to do, and the situation will be 100% resolved".

"I don't believe he has yet chosen a side in the Syrskyi matter. I spoke with him today and said that I am acting...
body.zh: 乌克兰多个城市爆发了抗议活动，抗议总统泽连斯基意外罢免受欢迎的国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫。 周四早上，一群人——大部分是年轻人——聚集在基辅，举着写着“放开费多罗夫”和“停止破坏胜利！”的牌子。并高喊“耻辱！”。 泽连斯基的决定引起了评论员、军方以及民间社会部分人士的极大不满。 有关费多罗夫任期结束与他与总司令亚历山大·西尔斯基之间的紧张关系有关的传言几乎得到了费多罗夫本人和泽连斯基的证实。 周四，费多罗夫透露，他已向泽伦斯基建议更换西尔斯基和总参谋长安德里·赫纳托夫。 泽连斯基在与英国首相凯尔·斯塔默举行的新闻发布会上承认，总参谋部和国防部之间的冲突是“系统性的”，并且发生在“各个层面”，西尔斯基和费多罗夫只会在他的调解下合作。 “当总统说他不打算取代西尔斯基时，我……说我会学习与他合作，”费多罗夫在自己的新闻发布会上说。但“我们提出的所有倡议都被阻止了，”他补充道。 费多罗夫谈到西尔斯基时说：“他没有找到一种不对称地击败俄罗斯的方法——这是总司令的工作——而是找到了一种分裂我们国家的方法。” 西尔斯基在 Telegram 上简短地写道，他对 2022 年俄罗斯军队逼近时在基辅周围开展的防御行动感到“自豪”，并表示他将继续“专注于战争和有效的战略”，然后祝愿费多罗夫“继续取得成功”。 35 岁的费多罗夫于 1 月份才被任命，但他被认为为该部注入了活力，领导了反腐败运动，并利用数据分析并试图提高一线绩效。 议员们定于周四就拟议的国防部长替换人选、现任内政部部长伊霍尔·克雷门科进行投票，但泽伦斯基表示，他只是正在考虑的人选之一，而且尚未提交任何正式提案。 作为泽伦斯基改组的一部分，在尤利娅·斯维里登科本周早些时候辞职后，议会批准任命国家石油和天然气公司老板谢尔盖·科列茨基为总理。 费多罗夫还透露，泽连斯基邀请他留在团队中担任顾问，但他拒绝了。 他解释说，他并不是想与总统对抗，并表示他“相信”泽伦斯基“听到了乌克兰人民的声音，知道该怎么做，问题将得到100%的解决”。 “我不相信他还没有在锡尔斯基事件中选择立场。我今天和他谈过，并说我正在采取行动......

reflection.en: When leaders make significant decisions without clear explanation, it can sow seeds of distrust and unrest among the populace. Proverbs 29:2 reminds us that the well-being of a nation is deeply tied to the integrity and transparency of its governance. Yahweh calls those in authority to act in ways that bring joy and stability, not confusion and dismay.

title.en: More than 800 Canadian wildfires burning as air quality alerts extend to US
title.zh: 空气质量警报延伸至美国 加拿大800多处山火在燃烧

summary.en: The air quality in large parts of Michigan, Minneapolis and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by authorities.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
More than 800 wildfires are burning across Canada, with air quality alerts now extending south into multiple US states.

The air quality in large parts of the northern states of Michigan and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by the US Air Quality Index program, with people recommended to stay indoors.

Alerts span the Upper Midwest, the Great Lakes region and into the northeast, the US national weather service (NOAA) said in an update on Thursday.

There are currently 857 fires actively burning in Canada, including 23 new fires on Thursday, according to the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre.

According to the Canadian Wildland Fire Information System, the vast majority of wildfires are burning out of control.

The large cluster of fires affecting northwestern areas of Ontario are responsible for sending thick plumes of smoke and poor air quality across Thunder Bay and Toronto, with lower concentrations of smoke high in the atmosphere drifting over the Great Lakes and above New York with hazy skies and redder sunrise and sunsets likely.

There will be quite widespread thunderstorms in Ontario over the next few days, but the rain may not be enough to make much of a difference.

Northwesterly winds will continue to blow the smoke into northern US states for the rest of this week and into the weekend, leading to concerns smoke will drift into New Jersey where Sunday's World Cup final is due to take place.

A change in the wind direction by Monday means that the smoke will tend to be steered across Quebec with an improvement in air quality further south in the US.

Air quality in the Midwestern city of Detroit is currently the worst in the world, Swiss air quality tracker IQAir said, followed by Minneapolis and Toronto.

Republican lawmakers in the state of Michigan have penned an open letter , external to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney asking for better management of the country's wildfires, expressing frustration for the third year in a row.

"A year has passed, the season has come around again, and nothing has changed except that our patience has run out," said the letter, signed by four House representatives from the US state.

Pete Hoekstra, the US ambassador to Canada, struck a more diplomatic tone in a statement on Wednesday commending wildfire fighting efforts from both countries.

"This challenge knows no borders. The United States will continue to coordinate closely with Canada, just as we have for more than four decades of shared wildfire emergencies," he said.

In addition to the hazardous smoke, the wildfires in northern Ontario have forced hundreds from local First Nations communities to evacuate, with videos showing some fleeing the remote area by boat.

Homes and buildings in the area have also been damaged extensively by the...
body.zh: 加拿大各地正在燃烧 800 多起野火，空气质量警报现已向南延伸至美国多个州。 美国空气质量指数计划将密歇根州和明尼苏达州北部大部分地区的空气质量视为“危险”，建议人们呆在室内。 美国国家气象局（NOAA）在周四的更新中表示，警报范围涵盖中西部北部、五大湖地区以及东北部。 据加拿大跨机构森林消防中心称，加拿大目前有 857 处正在燃烧的火灾，其中周四新增 23 处火灾。 根据加拿大荒地火灾信息系统，绝大多数山火正在失控燃烧。 影响安大略省西北部地区的大规模火灾导致雷湾和多伦多地区产生浓烟，空气质量较差，大气中较高浓度的烟雾飘过五大湖和纽约上空，天空朦胧，日出和日落可能会更红。 未来几天，安大略省将出现相当大范围的雷暴雨，但降雨可能不足以产生太大影响。 本周剩余时间和周末，西北风将继续将烟雾吹入美国北部各州，导致人们担心烟雾将飘入新泽西州，周日的世界杯决赛将在那里举行。 周一风向的变化意味着烟雾将倾向于穿过魁北克，而美国南部的空气质量将有所改善。 瑞士空气质量追踪机构 IQAir 表示，中西部城市底特律的空气质量目前是世界上最差的，其次是明尼阿波利斯和多伦多。 密歇根州的共和党议员向加拿大总理马克·卡尼发表了一封公开信，要求更好地管理该国的山火，连续第三年表达了失望之情。 这封由美国各州四名众议院代表签署的信中说：“一年过去了，季节又来了，除了我们的耐心已经耗尽之外，什么都没有改变。” 美国驻加拿大大使皮特·霍克斯特拉(Pete Hoekstra)周三在一份声明中采取了更为外交的语气，赞扬了两国的扑灭野火努力。 “这一挑战不分国界。美国将继续与加拿大密切协调，就像我们四十多年来共同应对野火紧急情况一样，”他说。 除了有害烟雾外，安大略省北部的野火还迫使当地原住民社区的数百人撤离，视频显示一些人乘船逃离偏远地区。 该地区的房屋和建筑物也受到严重破坏...

title.en: Algeria: Fire at orphanage kills 11, including children
title.zh: 阿尔及利亚：孤儿院火灾造成 11 人死亡，其中包括儿童

summary.en: A fire at an orphanage in the province of Algiers has killed 11 people and injured 19 more, authorities said. President Abdelmadjid Tebboune expressed his condolences amid his trip to Berlin.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 当局称，阿尔及尔省一家孤儿院发生火灾，已造成 11 人死亡、19 人受伤。总统阿卜杜勒马吉德·特本在柏林之行表示哀悼。 周四，当地人和急救人员赶往阿尔及尔省穆罕默迪亚区的一所孤儿院，应对大楼起火。 外门后面的两个窗户上方可以看到黑色的砖石，紧急服务人员聚集在外面。 阿尔及利亚当局表示，火灾已造成 11 人死亡、19 人受伤。 民防机构表示，十名伤者遭受不同程度的烧伤，急救人员帮助五名残疾人离开孤儿院，前往安全地带。 它最初没有提供有关受害者、他们的年龄或火灾可能原因的信息。 火灾似乎是在一夜之间爆发的，当地人称，他们第一次听到消防车的声音是在当地时间凌晨 3 点左右。 国家电视台播放了总理西菲·格里布在阿尔及尔两个医疗机构看望伤员的画面。 周四，阿尔及利亚总统阿卜杜勒马吉德·特布恩前​​往柏林与总统弗兰克·瓦尔特·施泰因迈尔和总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨举行会谈，他在社交媒体上发帖表达了哀悼。 特布恩说，他收到“儿童看护机构发生火灾，造成儿童死亡和其他人受伤的消息”。 阿尔及利亚经历了连续几天的酷暑，民防部门报告称，7 月 8 日至 15 日期间发生了 932 起火灾。 报告称，大部分已被扑灭，但少数仍在燃烧。 民防部门表示，已调动超过 19,000 名人员和 700 辆卡车以及 6 架直升机和 12 架水轰炸机来扑灭森林火灾。 阿尔及利亚北部每年夏天都会面临森林火灾，但干旱和气候变化加剧了这一现象。 几名嫌疑人也因涉嫌故意纵火而被捕。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

title.en: Why America's hospitals keep looking to India for nurses
title.zh: 为什么美国医院不断向印度寻找护士

summary.en: Thousands of Indian nurses aspire to work in the US, navigating yearslong visa backlogs to fill a growing healthcare workforce shortage.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Thousands of Indian nurses aspire to work in the US, navigating yearslong visa backlogs to fill a growing healthcare workforce shortage.

Angel Verghese, 25, has a clear plan. The nursing graduate from Welcare College of Nursing in Kochi in southern India's Kerala state has already passed the NCLEX, the US licensing exam for registered nurses.   

She is now gaining the work experience she needs before taking the IELTS English-language test and, she hopes, moving to New York, where her brother has already settled.

"I've always wanted to work in the US," Verghese told DW. "It offers better opportunities to learn, grow professionally and build a future. I know the process takes time, but I'm willing to wait."

Nearly 100 kilometers (62 miles) away in Kottayam, 26-year-old Susan Kurian is further along the same journey.

Having completed the clinical experience that US employers require, she is working with a recruitment agency to complete credential verification and secure a job offer from an American hospital.

"The paperwork is long and complicated, but my goal hasn't changed," Kurian told DW. "The US is where I want to build my career. I hope everything falls into place."

For thousands of young nurses across Kerala, the US remains the ultimate destination. The journey is rarely quick, often involving years of exams, paperwork and waiting, but the promise of better pay, career growth and international experience continues to draw them.

That demand is being fuelled by an American healthcare system struggling to find enough staff .

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects 189,100 registered nurse openings every year between 2024 and 2034, driven by an aging population and a wave of retirements.

Hospitals continue to recruit internationally, and India has become an increasingly important source of trained healthcare professionals.

Because Indian applicants face one of the longest employment-based immigration backlogs , nurses beginning the process today may have to wait more than a decade before receiving a US immigrant visa .

"Yes, we continue processing applications," Louie Terence, operations manager at Tiju's Academy, which prepares healthcare professionals for overseas licensing and language exams, told DW.

"Kerala nurses are well trained, speak good English and are known for their dedication. Many still see the US as the dream destination because of the salaries, working conditions and long-term career opportunities," said Terence.

title.en: The EU climate policy the world copied is under fire — what's at stake?
title.zh: 欧盟被全球效仿的气候政策正受到抨击——这预示着什么？

summary.en: The EU's emissions trading system (ETS), a global model for carbon pricing and CO2 reduction, is facing opposition from industry groups who are pushing back against stricter climate regulations. The debate centers on the scheme's effectiveness and its limitations.

body.en:
The emissions trading system became a global blueprint for pricing carbon and cutting CO2. Now industry groups are pushing back against tougher climate rules. How effective is the scheme and where does it fall short?

Europe's carbon market rarely makes headlines. But it has become one of the world's most influential climate policies.

The bloc wants to become carbon-neutral by 2050, and its carbon market is the central tool to meet that goal.

The European Commission is expected to present a proposal for the next revision of the European Emissions Trading System (ETS) shortly, and the question is whether that will make the system stronger or weaker.

Industrial frontrunners, including parts of Europe's steel sector that have already invested in cleaner production, are hoping for a stronger system. But what exactly is emissions trading, and how well does it work?

An emissions trading system (ETS) puts a price on pollution. Companies under the scheme must hold permits for the greenhouse gases they emit.

The European system covers aviation, oil refineries, coal-fired power stations, steelworks, cement, glass and paper production, as well as parts of the chemicals industry and shipping. Together, these sectors account for up to 40% of EU emissions, with roughly 10,000 industrial facilities, factories and power plants covered.

The idea is simple: the more a company pollutes, the more it should pay. The European Union sets an overall emissions cap and issues a limited number of allowances. Each permits the release of a specific quantity of greenhouse gases. These allowances can be traded on the carbon market.

This creates a carbon price that is designed to encourage companies to cut their emissions as quickly as possible. Revenues generated by the European system are intended to help finance the transition towards a greener economy. To keep the climate targets within reach, the emissions cap is reduced every year. Under the current rules, it falls annually by 4.3%.

According to the European Environment Agency, the EU's environmental authority, the strongest results have come in the energy sector. Emissions from all stationary industrial sites covered by the system fell by 51% between 2005 and 2024.

The energy-intensive steel industry now emits around 20% less than before the scheme began.

Aviation  tells a different story. According to the non-governmental organization Carbon Market Watch, emissions there continue to rise because the ETS captures only a small share of the sector's full climate impact .

One of the system's most powerful levers is also one of its central weaknesses: the free allocation of emissions allowances.

title.en: New Zealand downgrades tsunami alert for South Island after magnitude-5.9 earthquake

summary.en: Initially assessed as a magnitude-6.3 earthquake, NEMA later revised that downward to a 5.9.

body.en:
A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck near the town of Te Anau in New Zealand's South Island, shaking buildings and prompting authorities to briefly issue a tsunami warning.

The earthquake's epicentre was about 40km north of Te Anau, which is the gateway to the tourist hotspot of Fiordland, according to New Zealand's National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA). There were no immediate reports of injuries or damage.

The agency initially assessed the quake, which struck at 9.14pm local time (7.14pm AEST), at magnitude 6.3 before revising it downward to 5.9.

Although the tsunami alert was cancelled, NEMA said it expected coastal areas to experience "strong and unusual currents and unpredictable surges at the shore".

It said people should move out of the water, off beaches, and stay away from harbours, marinas and rivers.

title.en: What's behind the Iran regime's 'revenge propaganda'?
title.zh: 伊朗政权的“报复宣传”背后是什么？

summary.en: Calls for revenge over the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei are growing louder in Iran. Through increasingly harsh rhetoric, the leadership is seeking to mobilize supporters at home while warning opponents abroad.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Calls for revenge over the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei are growing louder in Iran. Through increasingly harsh rhetoric, the leadership is seeking to mobilize supporters at home while warning opponents abroad.

Since the funeral of Iran's slain supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, senior figures in the Islamic Republic have significantly escalated their rhetoric.   

Politicians, state-controlled media outlets and the country's new supreme leader have publicly called for retaliation to avenge Khamenei's death.

On July 14, at the first in-person session of Iran's parliament since the start of the war , lawmakers waved red flags bearing calls for revenge, according to images published by Iranian media. More than 180 of the parliament's 290 members endorsed demands for retaliation.

Pro-government media outlets have also promoted them aggressively. On Saturday, the conservative daily Hamshahri published what it described as a wanted list under the headline, "Retaliation Is Inevitable."

The list featured 13 Western politicians and military officials, including foreign and defense ministers, the commander of US Central Command (CENTCOM) and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

"These threats should not simply be dismissed as political rhetoric," legal scholar and human rights researcher Moein Khazaeli told DW. "At the same time, it is important to distinguish between the capability, the intention and the actual possibility of carrying out such threats."

Khazaeli said Iran's government was pursuing several objectives with its rhetoric. A significant part of the threats can be viewed as a form of psychological warfare and a strategy of deterrence, he said, adding that the regime is attempting to portray its weakened military and security apparatus as strong and operational.

The government is also signaling that it could resort to terrorist methods if international pressure continues — a threat that, given the Islamic Republic's history of overseas operations, cannot be dismissed outright, Khazaeli said.

The newspaper Hamshahri , which is owned by the Tehran municipality, is considered close to the conservative camp. It is among those within the Iranian establishment that strongly oppose negotiations with the United States and maintain close ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the country's most powerful military institution.

Iranian political activist Reza Alijani told DW that the mourning ceremonies for Ali Khamenei also served political purposes . Alijani said the leadership sought to instrumentalize the commemorations.

body.zh: 伊朗国内对阿亚图拉阿里·哈梅内伊之死进行报复的呼声越来越高。通过越来越严厉的言辞，领导层试图动员国内的支持者，同时警告国外的反对者。 自伊朗被杀最高领袖阿亚图拉·阿里·哈梅内伊的葬礼以来，伊斯兰共和国的高级人物的言论明显升级。 政界人士、国家控制的媒体和该国新任最高领导人公开呼吁进行报复，为哈梅内伊之死报仇。 伊朗媒体发布的图片显示，7 月 14 日，在伊朗议会自战争爆发以来的首次现场会议上，议员们挥舞着红旗，呼吁复仇。议会 290 名议员中有 180 多名支持报复要求。 亲政府媒体也大力宣传。周六，保守派日报《Hamshahri》以“报复不可避免”为标题发布了一份通缉名单。 该名单包括 13 名西方政治家和军事官员，其中包括外交部长和国防部长、美国中央司令部 (CENTCOM) 司令和德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨 (Friedrich Merz)。 法律学者兼人权研究员莫因·哈扎利 (Moein Khazaeli) 告诉德国之声：“这些威胁不应简单地被视为政治言论。” “与此同时，区分实施此类威胁的能力、意图和实际可能性也很重要。” 卡扎埃利表示，伊朗政府的言论是为了实现几个目标。他说，威胁的很大一部分可以被视为一种心理战和威慑战略，并补充说，该政权正试图将其被削弱的军事和安全机构描绘成强大且可操作的。 哈扎埃利表示，政府还表示，如果国际压力继续存在，它可能会诉诸恐怖手段——考虑到伊斯兰共和国的海外行动历史，这一威胁不能被彻底忽视。 德黑兰市政府拥有的《Hamshahri》报纸被认为接近保守派阵营。它是伊朗权力机构中强烈反对与美国谈判并与该国最强大军事机构伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）保持密切联系的人之一。 伊朗政治活动家礼萨·阿里贾尼告诉德国之声，阿里·哈梅内伊的哀悼仪式也有政治目的。阿利贾尼表示，领导层试图将纪念活动利用起来。 他说，这些活动旨在表明对执政机构的支持，转移人们对军事挫折的注意力，并使军事行动的继续合法化。

title.en: More than 500 feared dead after two boats sink near Myanmar
title.zh: 缅甸附近两艘船只沉没，恐有500多人遇难

summary.en: United Nations officials have issued warnings as over 500 people are feared dead after two boats sank near Myanmar. The incident occurred amidst severe torrential rain and widespread flooding in the region, which significantly increased the dangers of any sea travel.
summary.zh: 联合国发出警告，据信有500多人丧生，此前两艘船只在缅甸附近沉没。此次事件发生在该地区遭遇强降雨和洪水之际，恶劣天气大大增加了海上航行的危险。

body.en:
The United Nations warned on Thursday that more than 500 people were feared dead following reports of two large shipwrecks off Myanmar since late June.

The UN's International Organisation for Migration (IOM) and its High Commissioner for Refugees agency (UNHCR) voiced alarm in a joint statement at reports "that two boats carrying more than 500 people may have capsized off the coast of Myanmar in recent days".

Preliminary information indicated that the two vessels in question departed from war-torn Myanmar's Rakhine State in late June, with mainly members of the country's mostly Muslim Rohingya minority onboard, the statement said.

Some had reportedly travelled from the huge camps in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar , where more than a million Rohingya refugees who have fled from Rakhine live in squalid conditions.

The statement said that one boat, believed to have been carrying around 250 people, lost contact shortly after departure.

A second boat, reportedly carrying some 280 people, is meanwhile believed to have sunk off Myanmar's Ayeyarwady coast on 8 July.

"While the incidents and casualty figures have yet to be officially confirmed, UNHCR and IOM are gravely concerned by the potentially devastating loss of life," the statement said.

The UN agencies highlighted that the journeys "took place outside the regular sailing season, when maritime conditions are typically more hazardous".

"Recent torrential rain and flooding across the region have further increased the risks associated with such sea movements."

The statement cautioned that "if verified, this tragedy would add to the nearly 300 people reported to be missing or to have lost their lives in the Andaman Sea and Bay of Bengal so far this year, including Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals".

The Rohingya undertake perilous sea journeys every year in search of better living conditions, travelling aboard rickety boats often operated by trafficking networks.

According to UNHCR, nearly 900 Rohingya refugees were reported missing or dead at sea in the northern Indian Ocean last year alone — out of more than 6,500 who had attempted such perilous sea crossings.

title.en: In pictures: Orange skies and wildfire smoke loom over the World Cup final
title.zh: 橙色天空和野火烟雾笼罩世界杯决赛

summary.en: Wildfires have caused thick smoke to blanket major cities, leading to Canada recording the worst air quality globally, even as the smoke loomed over the World Cup final.
summary.zh: 随着浓烟笼罩主要城市，加拿大录得了全球最差的空气质量，甚至在世界杯决赛期间，烟雾也弥漫在空中。

body.en:
Canadians and some in the United States are being urged to stay indoors as wildfires continue to burn, creating chaos and tanking air quality across Canada and parts of the US, where the FIFA World Cup final is due to be played early next week.

Canadian authorities say crews are currently battling 110 out-of-control blazes, as more than 700 others continue to burn in remote areas. While not threatening major cities, the fires have burned 1.9 million hectares of land and are encroaching on smaller towns, prompting evacuation orders.

Smoke from the fires has blackened skies in Ontario and north-eastern parts of the US, prompting officials in both countries to cancel public events and issue health warnings.

In Ontario's capital Toronto — Canada's largest city — residents awoke to hazy, orange skies.

Officials have closed public pools, cancelled summer holiday programs and closed the official FIFA Fan Festival that had been planned to take place before the World Cup semi-final match between England and Argentina .

On Thursday, Swiss firm IQAir said the Canadian city recorded the worst air quality of any major city in the world, beating New Delhi and the Democratic Republic of Congo's capital Kinshasa.

Nearby, New York City's air quality ranked fifth-worst in the world. Authorities there have warned residents they "may see visible smoke and hazy skies across the state and spikes in smoke-related pollution".

The US National Weather Service said the smoke could linger into the end of the week.

"We probably haven't seen the worst of it yet for New York City. We probably haven't seen the worst of it yet for the Great Lakes and upstate and New England yet either," Dan Westervelt, Lamont associate research professor at Columbia University, told Reuters news agency.

The smoke settled on the city just days before neighbouring New Jersey is scheduled to host 80,000 people at an open-air stadium for the World Cup final on Monday morning AEST.

Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Maine and New Hampshire have all experienced worsened air quality.

The fires burn against the backdrop of a record-smashing North American heatwave, which has seen temperatures soar into the 40s in parts.

While significant, Canadian authorities say the current fire season has been significantly less dangerous than those that ravaged the country in 2023, when 18 million hectares burned.

— With additional reporting by Reuters news agency and Agence France-Presse.

title.en: Three times the size of Sydney's CBD: Why the US bombed this tiny island
title.zh: 三倍于悉尼中央商务区：美国为何轰炸这座小岛

summary.en: The United States conducted a 90-minute bombing attack on a small island, an action that has drawn attention to the expanding conflict over the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 美国对一个小岛进行了90分钟的轰炸，这一行动使人们关注到霍尔木兹海峡日益扩大的冲突。

body.en:
At the entrance to one of the world's most important shipping lanes, a tiny yet strategic Iranian island has become the latest target of the United States' strikes, hit by a 90-minute bombing campaign.

The US military said the attack on Iran's Greater Tunb Island, which sits alongside shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz, targeted "coastal defence systems and cruise missile storage".

The war in the Middle East has escalated into a new phase since last week, with the fragile ceasefire and memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the countries breaking down after commercial targets trying to pass the strait were attacked.

As part of the MoU , Iran agreed to provide a "safe passage" for the ships trying to pass the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil flows.

But now, with some vessels being targeted in the strait, the US says it has a new target to stop Iran's capabilities to target vessels in the region.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"What we've seen from the US during this phase of the conflict is that they are keen to suppress Iran's ability to target ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz," Jennifer Parker, an adjunct professor at the University of Western Australia's Defence and Security Institute, told SBS News.

"Their attacks in the last week, especially in the last 24 hours in Greater Tunb Island, for example, seem very specifically focused on Iran's ability to target ships in and around the strait."

Greater Tunb Island is a tiny island with a surface area of about 10 square kilometres, three times the size of the Sydney CBD, located in the eastern Persian Gulf, near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.

The island, seized by Iran from the United Arab Emirates in 1971, is a disputed territory, with the UAE claiming it belongs to them.

In May, Mohammad Akbarzadeh, deputy political officer of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy, told Iranian state television that the area that it uses to control the Strait of Hormuz "extends" as far as Greater Tunb Island.

Adel Abdel Ghafar, a Middle East expert and senior resident fellow at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute, said the island's location "alongside the inbound and outbound shipping lane" is "very strategic".

"Any [military] personnel or anti-ship cruise missiles based there are very close and can disrupt shipping and have disrupted shipping because the island is so close to the lane," he told SBS News.

"The islands really extend Iran's field of view and engagement from the mainland to the choke point itself.

The island's location is not the only reason experts believe it is important for Iran's control of the strait.

title.en: Hong Kong police raid two bookstores, arrest five people
title.zh: 香港警方突袭两家书店，逮捕五人

summary.en: Hong Kong police have arrested five booksellers and raided two independent bookstores, citing the sale of allegedly "seditious" publications. This action marks the latest step in an ongoing crackdown on independent bookshops in the city.
summary.zh: 香港警方逮捕了五名书商，并搜查了两家独立书店，理由是这些书店涉嫌销售“煽动性”出版物。此举是香港持续打击独立书店的最新行动。

body.en:
Five booksellers have been arrested in Hong Kong over the sale of allegedly "seditious" publications. Two bookstores have become the latest target in a continued crackdown on independent bookshops

Police in Hong Kong carried out raids on two bookshops, arresting five people under suspicion of displaying and selling seditious publications, reports said Wednesday.

The move marks a third round of arrests in a clampdown on independent bookstores, with similar operations conducted in March and June. 

The raids are widely seen as an attempt to crush free speech and dissent under the semi-autonomous city's stringent national security law .

According to media reports, police raided Have A Nice Stay bookshop —  founded by former journalists —  and Greenfield Book Store.

Footage shared by media outlets showed officers in vests marked with "Police" seizing boxes from  Have A Nice Stay while the AFP news agency said its reporters saw a woman in handcuffs being taken to the van from the store. 

Similar events were reported a few streets away, as boxes were carried out of the building that houses Greenfield Book Store, a video posted by  The Collective online news outlet showed.

A police statement later confirmed that two stores in Mong Kok district were raided, without naming the shops. 

The raid on Have A Nice Stay came a day after it announced in a Facebook post that it was shutting down on August  30, over reasons including "uncertainties regarding the social environment" and financial difficulties.

The police said the stores were searched by the National Security Department after customs officials alerted them to the discovery of allegedly seditious books in a shipment to Hong Kong from overseas.

The police statement said the publications' content included stirring up hatred against the city's government, judiciary and law enforcement agencies.

They said that the five people —  two men and three women —  were arrested on suspicion of violating the 2024 national security law.

The offense is punishable with up to seven years in prison under Hong Kong's national security law, which was enforced in 2024 on top of a 2020 legislation imposed by China after massive pro-democracy protests.

Hong Kong's independent bookstore industry once flourished, but it has dwindled since the enactment of the sweeping security law. 

In June, two employees of Hong Kong's Hunter bookstore were arrested, while four workers of the Book Punch were detained in March for selling "seditious" publications.

reflection.en: The raid on bookstores and arrest of booksellers in Hong Kong highlights the vulnerability of a people when rulers wield power without restraint. Yahweh's word reminds us that unchecked authority can be like a dangerous predator, causing distress and fear among the populace. title.en: 'I must get out into the free world', dissident who fled China on boat tells BBC
title.zh: “我必须进入自由世界”，乘船逃离中国的异议人士告诉BBC

summary.en: Dong Guangping, a Chinese dissident, shared with the BBC his dangerous journey by boat from China to South Korea, ultimately leading to his resettlement in Canada.
summary.zh: 中国异议人士董广平向BBC讲述了他从中国乘船逃往韩国的危险经历，最终他已在加拿大重新定居。

body.en:
As the rubber boat he was on rocked through choppy waves, fear washed over Chinese dissident Dong Guangping, who had gone without sleep for two days.

The 68-year-old knew he was taking a huge risk trying to flee China by sea, but even then, he had underestimated the challenges of this journey.

He was badly sunburned, his phone was running out of battery, and his portable charger had gone flat. Apart from the sky and the sea, there were no landmarks around him. He could only hope that the digital compass would get him to South Korea before his phone went flat.

"Not being able to navigate would have been terrifying. I could have drifted back towards China," Dong told BBC Chinese nearly two months after his perilous escape.

Forty hours after setting out from China's eastern Shandong province, Dong was rescued by the coast guard and fishermen in Korean waters on the night of 27 May.

He was briefly detained in South Korea but has since resettled in Canada, where his family had been living.

"I can never survive in China," said Dong, who spoke to BBC Chinese in a video call from Toronto.

"If I didn't leave, I will never be at peace for the rest of my life. I had to show the Chinese Communist Party I was capable of leaving. They cannot stop me, they cannot control me."

When asked for comment, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry told the BBC that the Chinese government "handles the entry and exit of its citizens in accordance with the law and that Chinese citizens must abide by the Constitution and the law".

Dong, a police officer-turned-human rights activist, has been jailed in China several times for his activism.

In 1999, Dong was fired from the police force after 13 years because he signed a petition to commemorate the 10th anniversary of the brutal Tiananmen crackdown on pro-democracy protesters .

Then in 2001, he was imprisoned for three years for "inciting subversion of state power". He was jailed again in 2014 for participating in another Tiananmen commemoration event, according to Amnesty International.

Dong had fled China four times previously but was sent back each time. "But I have always held fast to one conviction: I must get out into the free world," he tells BBC Chinese.

In September 2015, he travelled to Bangkok with his wife and daughter, where they were granted refugee status by the United Nations and approved for resettlement in Canada.

But days before they were scheduled to leave for Canada, Thai authorities deported Dong to China , where he was jailed for "inciting subversion" and "crossing the national border illegally". He was sentenced to three and a half years in jail.

body.zh: 当中国异见人士董广平乘坐的橡皮艇在波涛汹涌的海浪中摇晃时，他已经两天没有睡觉了。 这位68岁的老人知道他正冒着巨大的风险试图通过海路逃离中国，但即便如此，他还是低估了这段旅程的挑战。 他被严重晒伤，手机没电了，便携式充电器也没电了。除了天空和大海，他的周围没有任何地标。他只能希望数字指南针能在他的手机没电之前把他带到韩国。 “如果无法导航，那就太可怕了。我可能会漂回中国，”在危险逃亡近两个月后，董告诉 BBC 中文频道。 5月27日晚，董从中国东部山东省出发40小时后，在韩国海域被海警和渔民救起。 他在韩国被短暂拘留，但后来在加拿大定居，他的家人一直居住在那里。 “我永远无法在中国生存，”董在多伦多通过视频通话接受 BBC 中文版采访时说道。 “如果我不离开，我的余生都不会安宁。我必须向中国共产党证明我有能力离开。他们无法阻止我，他们无法控制我。” 当被问及置评时，中国外交部发言人告诉BBC，中国政府“依法办理公民出入境，中国公民必须遵守宪法和法律”。 董曾是一名警察，后来成为人权活动家，他在中国因其活动而多次入狱。 1999年，董因在一份请愿书上签名，纪念天安门残酷镇压民主抗议者10周年，在任职13年后被警察部队开除。 2001年，他因“煽动颠覆国家政权罪”被判入狱三年。据国际特赦组织称，2014 年，他因参加另一场天安门纪念活动而再次入狱。 此前，董曾四次逃离中国，但每次都被遣返。 “但我一直坚守一个信念：我必须走出去，进入自由世界，”他告诉BBC中文网。 2015年9月，他与妻子和女儿一起前往曼谷，在那里他们获得了联合国的难民身份，并获准在加拿大重新定居。 但在他们计划前往加拿大的前几天，泰国当局将董驱逐到中国，并以“煽动颠覆国家政权”和“非法越境”罪名入狱。他被判处三年半监禁。 2019年获释后，他再次试图游向台湾小岛金门越狱，但被中国人救起……

title.en: More people around the world now favour China over the US, Pew study suggests
title.zh: 皮尤研究显示，全球更多人青睐中国而非美国

summary.en: A Pew study indicates that more people globally now favor China over the United States, with greater confidence expressed in President Xi Jinping than in former President Donald Trump.
summary.zh: 皮尤研究中心的一项调查显示，目前全球更多人青睐中国而非美国，对习近平主席的信心也高于唐纳德·特朗普前总统。

body.en:
China is now viewed more positively than the US in many countries around the world, according to a new study by the Pew Research Center. It is the first time the organisation has recorded such results.

The findings from the non-partisan, US-based think tank indicate that favourable views of China have reached record highs in many countries, while perceptions of the United States have worsened.

In general, respondents expressed low confidence in both US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, though Xi scored higher than Trump.

While the US was still seen to respect personal freedoms more than China, China was seen to interfere in other countries' affairs less than the US.

Respondents were asked if they had a very favourable, somewhat favourable, somewhat unfavourable, or very unfavourable opinion of each superpower.

The research centre found that in 25 of the 36 countries, there were more people who had favourable views of China than of the US.

It marks the first time the centre, which has been tracking global sentiments towards the superpowers since 2002, has seen such a result in so many countries, according to Jonathan Schulman, one of the study's researchers.

Pew has seen previous dips in positive views of the US - in 2008, at the end of George Bush's administration, and in 2017, at the start of Trump's first term.

Even then, however, favourable views of China tended to be on par or slightly lower, Schulman told the BBC.

Spain, Indonesia, Italy, Greece and Canada were among the countries that saw the biggest swings towards China.

Only six countries in this year's survey still favour the US more, most of which are staunch US allies: Poland, the Philippines, South Korea, India, Japan and Israel.

Separately, the centre found that the median favourable opinion of the US across 20 countries had dropped steadily in recent years while the median favourable opinion of China had been rising.

Researchers also found that favourable views of China had increased in more than a third of the countries surveyed in recent years, based on an expanded dataset including the US.

And positive views of China reached record highs in some places surveyed this year, including Italy, Spain, Colombia, Mexico, Indonesia, Malaysia, Nigeria, and Turkey.

Researchers found that in general, middle-income countries tended to have positive views of China while wealthier countries tended to have more negative views.

One exception to this pattern was Singapore, which had the highest GDP per capita of the countries surveyed and a high level of positivity towards China.

The most positive - and the most negative - views of China in the survey came from the Asia-Pacific. About 90% of Pakistanis appear to favour China, while just 11% of Japanese do.

title.en: Five arrested after Hong Kong police raid independent bookshops
title.zh: 香港警方突击搜查独立书店后逮捕五人

summary.en: Hong Kong police have arrested five individuals following raids on independent bookshops, alleging they sold "seditious" books that incited "hatred" against authorities.
summary.zh: 香港警方突击搜查独立书店后逮捕了五人，指控他们涉嫌销售煽动对当局“仇恨”的“煽动性”书籍。

body.en:
Five people suspected of selling and displaying books deemed "seditious" in Hong Kong have been arrested after police raided two independent bookshops.

Authorities said the publications incited "hatred" against the territory's government, judiciary and law enforcement agencies. Officers seized books from both shops, the government said in a statement.

The group - two men aged 37 and 57, and three women aged between 30 and 59 - are suspected of violating national security legislation by "acting with seditious intent".

They are currently being held for investigation. If convicted, they could face up to seven years in prison.

Officials did not name the businesses raided by police. Reporters from the AFP news agency saw officers leading a woman in handcuffs the Have A Nice Stay bookshop into a van.

The shop in the city's densely packed Mong Kok area was founded in 2022 by a group of former journalists, stocking literature on democracy, authoritarianism and media literacy.

The raid came a day after it announced it would be shutting down in August, citing financial reasons and what it called an "elusive 'red line'" over what material is considered problematic.

On its Facebook page, the shop says it stocks books from Hong Kong and Taiwan, covering "literature, history, philosophy, art, sociology and self-improvement".

Neither business is attending this year's Hong Kong Book Fair, which opened on Wednesday.

There have been two other raids on bookshops in Hong Kong in 2026. Two workers were arrested at the Hunter store in June, and a further four were arrested from Book Punch in March.

Amnesty International said the raids indicated "the chilling reality of what the city has become: a place where you can be criminalised simply for what's on your bookshelf".

It said uncertainty over "so-called 'red lines'" had left booksellers and writers "guessing which titles could lead to criminal investigation, arrest or closure" - resulting in fear and self-censorship.
body.zh: 警方突袭两家独立书店后，五名涉嫌在香港出售和展示被视为“煽动”书籍的人被捕。 当局表示，这些出版物煽动了对该领土政府、司法和执法机构的“仇恨”。政府在一份声明中表示，警察从两家商店没收了书籍。 该团伙包括两名年龄在 37 岁和 57 岁之间的男性，以及三名年龄在 30 岁到 59 岁之间的女性，涉嫌“具有煽动意图”，违反国家安全法。 目前，他们已被拘留接受调查。如果罪名成立，他们可能面临最高七年的监禁。 官员们没有透露警方突击搜查的企业名称。法新社记者看到，警察将一名戴着手铐的妇女带进了一辆面包车。 这家商店位于香港人口稠密的旺角区，由一群前记者于 2022 年创立，出售有关民主、威权主义和媒体素养的书籍。 这次突袭是在该公司宣布将于 8 月份关闭的一天后进行的，理由是财务原因以及所谓的“难以捉摸的‘红线’”，即哪些材料被认为有问题。 该书店在其Facebook页面上称，其库存来自香港和台湾的书籍，涵盖“文学、历史、哲学、艺术、社会学和自我提升”。 两家公司都没有参加今年于周三开幕的香港书展。 2026 年，香港还发生了两起针对书店的突袭行动。6 月，Hunter 书店有两名员工被捕，3 月 Book Punch 又有四名员工被捕。 国际特赦组织表示，这次突袭表明“这座城市已经变成了一个令人毛骨悚然的现实：一个你可能仅仅因为书架上的东西就被定罪的地方”。 报告称，“所谓‘红线’”的不确定性让书商和作家“猜测哪些书名可能导致刑事调查、逮捕或关闭”，从而导致恐惧和自我审查。

reflection.en: When authorities use their power to suppress ideas and silence voices, it can feel like a heavy burden on the people. summary.en: China's economy grew by 4.3% in the three months to June, a figure lower than expected and one of its lowest quarterly rates on record, raising concerns about the economy's balance.

body.en: Worse-than-expected figures for three months to June come amid concerns over lopsided economy Business live – latest updates China has posted worse-than-expected growth figures for the three months to June as its economy expanded by just 4.3% – one of its lowest quarterly readings on record. The rate, which came in under the government’s target of 4.5% to 5%, was one of the weakest since reporting on official quarterly GDP figures began in the early 1990s. Continue reading...

reflection.en: Economic reports often focus on human strategies and market forces, yet this news reminds us that true prosperity ultimately comes from Yahweh. Youlin Chen – who has researched how to detect underground nuclear tests using seismological data – was detained on 5 November 2024, according to a statement from the NGO Global Reach, which is working with his family to secure his freedom. Continue reading...

body.en: Covert footage obtained by the Guardian shows how crime networks are using souvenir shops to hide a booming wildlife trade targeted at a new influx of Chinese tourists The shop is dark and deserted. Though the door is open, there is clearly no expectation of any customers walking in off the street. Visits are likely by appointment and from a specific clientele. This shop is part of an organised crime network. What is being sold is highly illegal and incredibly unethical. Anyone wandering in would see large bags of specialist tea, local coffee, trinkets and cigarettes on the shelves. But the photographs of wild animals adorning the walls offer a clue to what is truly for sale here. Continue reading...

title.en: One mistaken sighting created an enduring myth about this Aussie animal

summary.en: It has been credited with soaring 100 metres. But new research suggests the greater glider's reputation was overblown.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In 1941 in Milton, a village in southern NSW, a local reported seeing a greater glider, a native 'flying marsupial', soar through the night air to land 100m away.

The one sighting launched a pervasive myth about the abilities of the greater glider, one of 10 glider species native to Australia.

"It was a misidentification that has carried on for many decades, and there actually just is no dataset or empirical measurements," Dr Ana Gracanin told SBS News.

Gracanin, a researcher with the Fenner School of Environment and Society at the Australian National University, set out with a team to measure the greater glider's glide distance for the first time.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The southern greater glider, named 'great' because of its size, soared an average of only 19.1m, or less than a quarter the distance it was once assumed.

The researchers say their findings have big implications for the conservation of the endangered species.

Gracanin spent hours in the forest at night with infrared cameras and torches, becoming familiar with the individual gliders and their favourite tree dents.

"My friends have a joke because they all look very similar ... whenever there's a glider, we'd be like 'It's Gary! We have a Gary!'"

It's unclear what the total population of southern greater gliders is, but scientists estimate their population declined by 80 per cent after the Black Summer bushfires.

"Often they're very high up in the canopies, but if you put your binoculars to your eyes you can very quickly tell if it's a greater glider," Gracinan said.

"It has huge fluffy ears, a very funny gremlin-y face, and they have a very long fluffy tail ... They're just a big ball of fluff."

Recording data on the southern greater gliders' movements for the first time, Gracinan and her team found they climbed an average of 22m before launching themselves at a 43.5 degree angle at a nearby tree.

"It kind of goes into a Superman pose and has its hands under its chin ... like a black furry flying carpet shape that goes through the sky, and the tail is spinning left, right, left to stabilize."

The longest glide they recorded was 47m. But the average distance was well short of that, at 19.1m.

The distance fell short of the glider record, which was set by a yellow-bellied glider which travelled 145m.

The southern greater glider's inability to glide long distances puts them at greater risk of becoming isolated from the rest of the population, and of extinction.

"They're restricted to their little territories, their gliding ability and their diet," Gracanin said.

title.en: Australian patient details exposed in GP network cyberattack
title.zh: 澳大利亚全科医生网络遭网络攻击，患者信息泄露

summary.en: Partnered Health announced that a cybersecurity breach has exposed patient details from 21 clinics across several Australian cities.

body.en:
Thousands of medical records and patient information stored with a giant healthcare provider have been breached in a cyber attack.

Partnered Health, owned by private equity firm Quadrant, said 21 clinics across several cities including Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra have been affected by the breach on 23 June.

"Our investigations to date have confirmed that personal information (including health information) was taken from some of the clinics in our network," the healthcare provider said on Wednesday.

"As a health services provider, we know our patients and our people trust us with personal and medical information, and we sincerely apologise for any concern and inconvenience this may cause them."

The healthcare group said "a malicious actor" accessed the data, prompting it to report the incident to the Australian Cyber Security Centre, the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, and law enforcement.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Personal information stolen included names, dates of birth, addresses and contact details as well as Medicare, private health insurance and concession card details.

Medical information and treatment details, including consultation notes, referral letters, and pathology or diagnostic results recorded by a GP were also breached.

The medical group has sought an interim injunction from the Supreme Court of NSW ordering that the accessed data is not used or published.

Established in 2013, Partnered Health has more than 60 medical centres nationwide as well as skin cancer, allied health and mental health clinics, with its services reaching more than five million people.

Health insurer Bupa announced in June it was acquiring Partnered Health, the latest major business to be struck by hackers.

Data breach notifications to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner reached a record high in 2025, with major incidents including a cyberattack on Qantas that compromised the details of 5.7 million customers and reportedly leaked on the dark web.

The office said it received 1205 data breach notifications in the 2025 calendar year, representing an eight per cent increase from 2024.

title.en: Deadly avian flu detected in New Zealand for the first time
title.zh: 新西兰首次发现致命禽流感

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
New Zealand has reported its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu after a migratory seabird found on a ‌beach near Wellington tested positive.

The case in a ‌brown skua seabird comes after the virus was detected in June in Australia , the last continent to ‌report the virus.

The virulent H5 strain has spread through wild bird and mammal populations since 2021, killing millions and infecting poultry and dairy farms as well as some farm workers.

"There is no evidence of any mass mortality in wildlife or transmission between wild birds in New Zealand. There has been no detection ‌in poultry," Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard said in ⁠a statement on Wednesday.

Hoggard said New Zealand might see a similar pattern to cases reported in Australia , where there have been 14 confirmed or presumed positive detections of H5 bird flu as of Wednesday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

New Zealand has been preparing for the arrival of H5N1, working with the poultry industry to develop biosecurity and resilience plans.

New Zealand's wild birds are unusually vulnerable because they evolved for millions ⁠of years without native land mammals, leaving many species ‌flightless, ground-nesting and poorly equipped to defend themselves against predators.

That isolation made them unique but also left them highly exposed to habitat ‌loss and introduced pests such as stoats, rats and feral cats.

Many species are already endangered, putting them at great risk of extinction if the virus spreads rapidly.

Health officials have started a vaccination program for 300 core breeding birds from five of the country's most endangered species, including flightless takahe and kakapo.

Brett Gartrell, professor of wildlife health at Massey University, told Reuters ‌he was worried that bird flu could push some of the country's critically endangered birds to extinction.

"We are incredibly worried about New Zealand's biodiversity because our birds have never had to deal with anything like this before," Gartrell said.

"If it spreads quickly in New Zealand, we could be in trouble ... those core group of birds that (officials) want to protect with the vaccination won't be fully immune if it spreads too quickly."

title.en: Australia is changing course on AI — but key questions remain
title.zh: 澳大利亚正在改变人工智能方向——但关键问题仍然存在

summary.en: Labor wants to accelerate AI investment while protecting households, workers and creators — but crucial details are still to come.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's shift towards tougher artificial intelligence regulation has been broadly welcomed, but pressure is building for more detail and decisive action on the risks posed by the technology.

Albanese announced on Wednesday the federal government would legislate a set of AI standards next year, including new requirements for data centres to underwrite energy generation and pay for additional water use.

An AI office would be created within Albanese's department, while national standards would cover education and training, workplace rights and productivity. The government also wants to fast-track AI investment in Australia.

The announcement marks a shift away from the federal government's previous light-touch approach to regulation, and comes after months of pressure from both the tech industry and those worried about the rapid shifts of AI on the economy.

But the prime minister provided few details about the proposals which he vowed to legislate by early 2027 after a national cabinet process with state and territory leaders.

Albanese said getting the framework right would enable faster approvals and make Australia a more attractive destination for international investors.

"It is not our goal to try and legislate for every possible eventuality or risk," he said.

Monash University AI researcher Geoff Webb labelled the AI office an "important initiative" that would bolster Australia's capacity to pursue "critical" sovereign AI capabilities.

Digital Rights Watch chair Lizzie O'Shea also backed the move but was concerned fast-tracking AI data centre approvals could exacerbate community mistrust in AI.

"[By] prioritising data centres, we lose capacity to build out renewable energy projects in the climate crisis, new home construction in the housing crisis, and we likely increase the current cost of electricity and water in a cost of living crisis," O'Shea said.

But Greens senator David Shoebridge was critical, saying the office would not have statutory powers.

"What the prime minister has offered today is a single door in his office," he said. "That is not going to deliver the protections Australians have been asking for."

Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said the office would create “more bureaucracy” and hinder Australia’s adoption of the technology.

The government released expectations for large AI data centres in March, but Albanese said these would now be strengthened through legislation.

Developers would be required to underwrite new power generation for the energy-intensive facilities and pay for additional water use.
